comparison: Both evaluate in vivo senescence markers (C11-C15). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with multiple orthogonal methods. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising concerns that markers could reflect inflammation rather than senescence due to Doxo's systemic effects, requesting additional confirmation like beta-gal staining in tissue sections.

OpenEval R1 includes in vitro C2C12 senescence markers (C16-C21) as part of comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation. Peer R2 rates these same claims UNSUPPORTED, fundamentally questioning C2C12 as a senescence model due to deleted p16/p19 locus and immortalized nature, recommending primary myoblasts instead.

Both evaluate PGD2 pathway enzyme expression and 15d-PGJ2 release (C22-C27). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong qPCR and mass spec data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether increases are due to senescence or DNA damage, recommending alternative senescence models and noting only two replicates for mass spec.

Both evaluate conditioned medium effects on differentiation (C30-C33). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate rescue experiments. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, identifying critical missing control: conditioned medium from non-senescent proliferative cells needed to confirm effect is specific to senescent cells.

OpenEval R4 evaluates proliferation effects (C34-C36) as SUPPORTED but notes concentration concerns. Peer R5 evaluates both proliferation and differentiation effects (C34-C42) as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing inability to distinguish cytotoxicity from specific differentiation inhibition, requesting cell count, division, and death data.

OpenEval R5 evaluates differentiation inhibition (C37-C42) as SUPPORTED with multiple orthogonal methods. Peer R5 includes these claims in UNCERTAIN evaluation, raising concerns about toxicity confounding differentiation effects and lack of delineation between toxic and specific effects.

Both evaluate HRas C184 modification by 15d-PGJ2 (C44-C47). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises experimental design with cysteine mutants. Peer reviewers acknowledge clear data showing negative role and HRas modification, though noting the interaction was previously reported in other cell types.

Both evaluate FRET data showing HRas activation (C48-C51). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong evidence with appropriate controls but lacks cell number reporting. Peer reviewers accept the FRET analysis and cysteine-dependence without methodological concerns.

Both evaluate differential MAPK vs PI3K pathway activation (C52-C56). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with elegant controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not challenging the selectivity but questioning physiological relevance due to high concentrations causing near-complete cell death and minimal ERK phosphorylation increase.

Both evaluate HRas redistribution to plasma membrane (C59-C61). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes modest 20% change. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising critical concern that Golgi accumulation in mutants could be due to defective palmitoylation rather than lack of 15d-PGJ2 modification, requesting direct palmitoylation comparison.

Both evaluate C184S rescue of differentiation (C63-C66). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes incomplete rescue. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, identifying fundamental flaw: overexpression doesn't account for endogenous HRas; knockout/knockdown or knock-in mutations needed to definitively establish C184 dependence.

Both evaluate HRas localization-function relationship using V12 mutants (C128-C130). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the paradox that Golgi-localized active HRas doesn't inhibit differentiation. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting data without specific concerns.

OpenEval R12 synthesizes overall mechanistic conclusions (C87-C90) as SUPPORTED but notes reliance on correlative evidence and lack of in vivo rescue. Peer R3 includes C87 in evaluation of PGD2 pathway, rating UNCERTAIN due to DNA damage vs senescence ambiguity.

OpenEval R12 includes integrated conclusion about mechanism (C89). Peer R10 includes C89 in evaluation of rescue experiments rated UNSUPPORTED due to overexpression approach limitations. Both recognize gaps in establishing causal chain.

OpenEval R17 evaluates pathway selectivity conclusions (C111-C112, C115) as SUPPORTED but notes C115 is speculative without direct rescue experiments. Peer R8 includes C111-C112 in UNCERTAIN evaluation focused on concentration and physiological relevance concerns.

OpenEval R18 evaluates mechanistic model of HRas redistribution (C118, C120-C122) as SUPPORTED but notes inference rather than direct demonstration. Peer R9 includes these claims in UNCERTAIN evaluation, emphasizing missing direct evidence linking C184 modification to C181 palmitoylation.

OpenEval R19 evaluates localization-function link (C127) as SUPPORTED but notes interpretive complications with constitutively active mutants. Peer R11 includes C127 in SUPPORTED evaluation of supplementary data without specific concerns.
OpenEval R13 evaluates background/context claims (C1, C67-C78) as SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval R14 evaluates extensive background claims (C2, C28, C43, C57-C58, C79-C137) as SUPPORTED by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval R15 evaluates prior work citations (C29, C62) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature references.
OpenEval R16 evaluates Doxo-induced senescence in MCF7 cells (C93) as SUPPORTED, noting generalizability. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this supporting observation.

OpenEval R20 evaluates therapeutic implications (C138-C140) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of in vivo rescue experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing therapeutic potential claims.

Peer R4 includes claims C4-C5 in evaluation of conditioned medium experiments, which are not explicitly evaluated in any OpenEval result. These appear to be contextual claims related to the experimental design.
